text: The Rust programming language was created by Graydon Hoare at Mozilla Research as a personal project in 2006. After years of development, Mozilla officially sponsored Rust in 2009, and version 1.0 was released in 2015. The language's borrow checker enforces ownership rules at compile time, eliminating data races without a garbage collector. Rust was adopted by Linux Torvalds into the Linux kernel in 2022, making it the second language after C approved for kernel development. Amazon Web Services uses Rust in its Firecracker virtualization layer, and Microsoft is rewriting critical Windows components in Rust to address memory safety vulnerabilities. The Rust Foundation, established in 2021 with backing from Google, Microsoft, AWS, and Huawei, now governs the language's development.
